title: Why Is FICO Stock Crashing, and is it a Generational Buying Opportunity?
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc's September 23 video answers his own headline directly: yes, the ~45% year-to-date crash in Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) is a high-conviction buying opportunity. The selloff is driven by mortgage-scoring regulation risk and a VantageScore policy shift that threaten FICO's historically iron grip on credit scoring for home loans; a further headline is FICO expanding TENT access for FHA lenders, which supports adoption but limits pricing power. His counterargument is business quality: trailing-12-month revenue of $2.4 billion (up from ~$500 million in 2017), revenue growth above 20% even in the latest quarter, operating margins of 52% (up from ~20% in 2017), and return on invested capital of 56.5%, roughly five times its weighted average cost of capital. The stock now trades at a 17.5x forward P/E, the cheapest in a very long time, after years at super-premium multiples. He updated his discounted cash flow model and puts fair value at $1,153 per share, about 24% above the current price, projecting that upside over 12-18 months. The call: FICO — BUY with high conviction, his highest conviction tier (low/medium/high), for long-term investors willing to take the risk that regulatory change permanently erodes the pricing-power moat. Base/bull: the moat persists and the multiple re-rates as policy fears prove overblown; bear: regulation strips pricing power and the elite margins compress. Other tickers: none discussed. The video carries a Motley Fool sponsorship; one auto-caption spot garbles a short phrase ('expanding TENT access') without changing meaning.
